I will keep my farm simple and steady this year because I am 78, my household is small, and I have to manage work that I can actually finish on time. I will put most of my land into the wheat-maize rotation because that is the system I know best, it matches my land and irrigation conditions, and it gives me stable grain production. I will keep a smaller piece in cotton because I already grow it and I want some cash income, but I will not expand it because cotton needs more hand work and more spraying. On wheat, I will use improved seed, moderate fertilizer, and several irrigations from my well so I can protect yield without making the season too costly. After wheat harvest, I will put hybrid maize on the same land and use no-tillage or very light tillage to save labor and catch the summer season quickly. For cotton, I will manage it more carefully with more pesticide sprays than grain crops because insects are a bigger risk there. Overall, I will choose a balanced input level: not the highest, but enough to protect output and keep the work within my strength.
